login: Force crashpad on kukui Force kukui devices to start using crashpad immediately. Breakpad does not work on kukui devices such as Krane. We are losing crash reports from Chrome browser processes, and other Chrome crash reports are corrupt and unusable. This is a launch blocker for Krane; we don't know if there are stability issues. Crashpad does not have the same issues as breakpad on these devices. We want to move to crashpad eventually anyways, so rather than trying to fix the deprecated breakpad, let's move to crashpad on kukui. There are no released kukui devices, so this only affects testers. Other devices do not have the same issues with breakpad, so we can do a slower rollout & dogfooding for everything else in later CLs. This is just the emergency switchover for kukui. BUG=chromium:1001139 TEST=On a Krane. kill -SEGV main chrome process. Visit chrome://crash, chrome://gpucrash, and chrome://inducebrowsercrashforrealz. All produce crash reports. cros-disks: Force unmount network FUSE filesystems on EBUSY Unmounting filesystems will fail if it is being accessed. However, for drivefs and sshfs, there's no action a user can take to recover from such an error. Since these are FUSE filesystems, MNT_FORCE can be used to unmount the filesystem. FROMLIST: firmware: google: increment VPD key_len properly Commit 4b708b7b1a2c ("firmware: google: check if size is valid when decoding VPD data") adds length checks, but the new vpd_decode_entry() function botched the logic -- it adds the key length twice, instead of adding the key and value lengths separately. On my local system, this means vpd.c's vpd_section_create_attribs() hits an error case after the first attribute it parses, since it's no longer looking at the correct offset. With this patch, I'm back to seeing all the correct attributes in /sys/firmware/vpd/... FROMLIST: ALSA: core: Fix card races between register and disconnect commit 2a3f7221acddfe1caa9ff09b3a8158c39b2fdeac upstream. There is a small race window in the card disconnection code that allows the registration of another card with the very same card id. This leads to a warning in procfs creation as caught by syzkaller. The problem is that we delete snd_cards and snd_cards_lock entries at the very beginning of the disconnection procedure. This makes the slot available to be assigned for another card object while the disconnection procedure is being processed. Then it becomes possible to issue a procfs registration with the existing file name although we check the conflict beforehand. The fix is simply to move the snd_cards and snd_cards_lock clearances at the end of the disconnection procedure. The references to these entries are merely either from the global proc files like /proc/asound/cards or from the card registration / disconnection, so it should be fine to shift at the very end. init: fix incorrect result from GetBlockCount The GetBlockCount helper function falls back to checking /sys/class/block/[dev]/size to get a count of blocks if dumpe2fs fails. However, that interface returns a count of sectors (512 bytes) instead of blocks (often 4096 bytes). This means that if we do get the block count from this fallback, our count will be 8 times too large. This causes an error message when we attempt to write beyond the size of the file system. Add block size as a parameter to GetBlockCount, so that we can convert the sector count into a block count.
